results.content: Both resin and plastic products manufacturing supply chains have remained unaltered because of tariffs. This may not be surprising considering that trade flows, as the percentage of domestic shipments for resin and plastic products imports in 2024, were 17.4% and 20.5%, respectively, as shown in the recently released 2025 Global Trends Report on plastics trade.\ Plastics equipment and molds for plastic production imports, on the other hand, had trade flows as a percentage of domestic shipments [...] When the U.S. announced higher tariffs on imports in the spring of this year, one of the main concerns was their impact on the industry supply chain. Should imports become more expensive, it might slow the flow of goods into the U.S.—and where tariffs are excessive—it could have significant adverse effects on supply chains, not only in the U.S. but globally. As of July 2025, the value of U.S. imports of plastic materials and resins, plastic products, plastics machinery, and molds decreased 1.0% [...] domestic shipments of 68.8% and 93.0%, respectively, which suggests that higher tariff rates on both could have a greater likelihood of causing supply chain disruptions. However, this has not happened so far, given that the capacity utilization rate in plastic products manufacturing has been low—meaning there is sufficient capacity to tap should supply chain disruptions occur via equipment and molds. results.title: Tariffs in Plastics Manufacturing: Quantifying and Mitigating ...
results.content:
If enacted, recently proposed tariffs will add extra duties to many plastic-related goods entering the U.S., spanning raw materials, components and subassemblies, finished parts, as well as machinery and equipment. These tariffs were introduced under various trade measures (e.g., Sections 301 and 232) targeting specific countries or product categories. Plastics manufacturers must stay vigilant in tracking exemptions, adjustments, and expirations that can significantly impact supply chains and [...] Cross-Border Supply Chains: Even if a company does not import materials directly (i.e., the company purchases from a domestic supplier rather than sourcing from overseas), second- or third-tier suppliers could be importing components or raw materials subject to tariffs, and as a result, may pass on their own tariff-related price increases.

#### Potential Consequences [...] ### Key Takeaways

 Tariffs disrupt costs, profitability, and supply chains in plastics manufacturing.
 Effective modeling of tariff exposure is essential for M&A and strategic decisions.
 Mitigation strategies include supply chain diversification and contractual hedging.
 Automation and partnerships can reduce tariff-related cost pressures.
 Working with an experienced advisor ensures better valuation and trade risk management.
